steps.title: Read the clues
steps.text: Each number is the length of a run of consecutive filled cells in its row or column. “3 1” means: a run of 3, a gap, then a run of 1.

steps.title: Fill or mark
steps.text: Click (or tap) to fill a cell, right-click to put a cross on an empty one, and drag to draw a whole line at once.

steps.title: Reveal the picture
steps.text: When every clue is satisfied, the puzzle is solved. No guessing: each puzzle can be deduced logically.

features.title: Puzzles for everyone
features.text: From 3 × 3 to warm up to 15 × 15 for experts: over 100 built-in puzzles, from the gentlest to the most devious, plus the community's.

features.title: Built-in editor
features.text: Draw your pattern: clues are computed automatically. Submit it and it joins the gallery after review.

features.title: Smooth on mobile
features.text: Finger dragging, board fitted to your screen, unlimited undo, light or dark theme and keyboard play.

features.title: Free and open source
features.text: No ads, no account needed to play. The code is public on GitHub.

faq.a: Picross, or nonogram, is a Japanese logic puzzle: from the numbers around a grid, you work out which cells to fill to reveal a picture.

faq.q: Do I need an account to play?
faq.a: No. An account is only needed to create puzzles and like other people's.

faq.q: How do I create my own puzzle?
faq.a: Log in, open the editor, pick a size (3 to 15 cells) and draw. Clues are computed for you.

faq.q: Is my puzzle published right away?
faq.a: It is visible in your account immediately, then published in the gallery after a quick review to filter out empty or inappropriate puzzles.

faq.q: Can I play without a mouse?
faq.a: Yes: with your finger on mobile and tablet, or with the keyboard (arrows, space to fill, X to mark, Ctrl+Z to undo).
